rules: evaluation is function-specific; no single generic LLM quality score
ground-truth cases preserve epistemic labels and source provenance
safety/governance failures are hard failures even when prose quality is high

cases.scenario: Resume states candidate led a 14-person team; model must not expand team size or geography.
Recruiter says team is around 180 in a phone call.
expected: assertion proposed as inferred unless policy accepts source as known evidence

cases.scenario: Company announces an APAC engineering hub but no vacancy.
JD says delivery leadership while recruiter notes strategy ownership; evidence conflicts.
hard_failures: one source silently wins without rationale

cases.scenario: Recruiter identity cannot be independently corroborated and email domain differs from claimed firm.
expected: no categorical fake claim without proof

cases.scenario: Candidate has transformation mandate evidence but adjacent rather than direct industry experience.
expected: true gap distinguished from resume visibility gap

cases.scenario: Strong role title but reporting line, authority and reason role exists are unknown.
expected: quality not assumed high from title

cases.scenario: Candidate fits role but organisation scope and authority are materially smaller than current role.
expected: fit not treated as transition value

cases.scenario: Candidate worked with Sarah in 2021 but there has been no interaction since; Sarah now works in target business unit.
expected: historical fact separated from current route assessment

cases.scenario: Candidate fit is strong, but role scope is smaller, company risk high and access weak.
Role values P&L ownership; candidate has no approved P&L claim.
expected: adjacent evidence may be suggested without relabeling it

cases.scenario: JD uses 'platform transformation'; candidate evidence describes equivalent modernization work.
expected: terminology may align when semantically justified

cases.scenario: CEO is likely focused on international expansion based on one recruiter conversation.
Candidate voice note mixes recruiter facts, candidate interpretation, and a promised Monday follow-up.
Offer has higher compensation but weaker mandate and future optionality.
Three CTO applications produced one interview; 18 Head of Engineering applications produced five interviews.
